training.case_control_note: no-event loan-months subsampled at 10% with weight 10

overlay.rule: realized / predicted hazard on held-out loans over the window; applied to a cause only if the out-of-time protocol showed the overlay carries forward for it and the ratio is more than two standard errors from 1

limitations: Default means the first month 90 or more days past due (or REO, or an adverse termination). Most such loans later cure or are repaid from a sale; that is why loss given default is small, and why COVID-19 forbearance shows up as a wave of defaults.

The only housing downturn in the data is the one the 2006-2008 vintages lived through (their months to 2016-12); the 2017-2026 sample contains none. The response to falling prices and to loans under water therefore rests on one downturn and on loans originated just before it: the training rows span 12-month changes in state house prices from -20% and mark-to-market LTV up to 122%. It has not been tested on a second downturn. The engine reports every month in which a driver leaves the training range.

Loans are observed for at most about eleven years (the 2006-2008 vintages, to 2016-12; the 2017-2026 sample for at most nine), and 99.5% of the training months lie within 107 months of origination. Beyond that the hazard's dependence on loan age is held at its last fitted level, so lifetime figures for long-dated loans rest on that assumption.

One stress episode (2020-06 to 2022-06) defines the stressed regime, and the regime chain is estimated from 99 months: the expected stress spell (25 months) and the long-run stressed share (26%) are uncertain, and the baseline lifetime PD inherits that uncertainty. The regime series starts in 2017, so 2008-2012 is not labelled stressed: that downturn reaches the hazards through house prices, unemployment and mark-to-market LTV, and a scenario's forced stress months add the COVID-type effect only.
The model conditions on origination attributes and macro drivers, not on a loan's current delinquency status, so it understates the risk of a loan that is already past due.
The property's state is a feature. Geography can stand in for protected characteristics, so a lender using these figures in credit decisions must test for disparate impact on its own portfolio.

Prepayment drift follows the rate cycle and can reverse. In this export's out-of-time protocol a correction carried forward, narrowly (later months moved from 0.942 to 0.952 of realized), so the prepayment hazard is scaled by 0.9810; in the previous export (2017-2026 only) the same test failed and no scalar was applied.
Trained on agency-conforming fixed-rate mortgages; not validated for other products.
target: first month 90+ days past due, REO acquisition or adverse zero-balance termination (default); zero-balance payoff (prepayment)
population: Freddie Mac single-family fixed-rate loans, random sample of 40,000 loans per origination quarter: 2017-2026, and 2006-2008 followed to 2016-12
algorithm: LightGBM multiclass gradient-boosted trees on loan-months (discrete-time competing-risks hazard)
